source: PM Sánchez, Congress address (Sep 3) / House of Commons Library
note: Figure rose from 72 (Aug 2) to 86 (Sky News) to 111 by Aug 3-4, then to 141 as cited by PM Sánchez in his Sep 3 Congress address without a detailed methodology for the new count; not all later-recovered bodies definitively linked to the July crisis. The new official figure coincidentally matches the NGO (Caminando Fronteras) tally from Aug 5 (see below), though officials have not confirmed they share the same underlying data. A one-month retrospective (The Olive Press, Aug 30) had already cited 'more than 150' — the highest figure reported to date (see below).

78 bodies recovered in Spanish waters, 63 in Moroccan waters, per hospital/morgue monitoring across northern Morocco. Spanish officials confirmed the figures to Cadena SER without formally adopting them as the state count; deaths were classified under Spain's 'multiple victims' mass-casualty protocol, a first for this type of incident. Moroccan authorities have not officially confirmed the NGO tally, and the number of people still missing remains unknown.
Majority of confirmed fatalities occurred on the Spanish side, concentrated at the Tarajal and Benzú breakwaters.
Remaining confirmed fatalities occurred on the Moroccan side of the border during the same crossing period.
Distinct tally cited specifically for drownings during the peak Jul 30-Aug 1 crossing window; overlaps substantially but not fully reconciled with the cumulative 111 figure.
Prompted a €25M emergency fund and mainland transfers; UNICEF and Save the Children both flagged trafficking and protection risk.

category: Alleged sexual assault cases under Civil Guard investigation
note: Includes one arrest of a man with prior terrorism-related offences; investigations remained open as of Aug 15.
Reported independently of the Civil Guard's 15-case tally; degree of overlap between the two figures not established.

injured: 700+ held in 512-capacity centre; hundreds more outside without food or water for days
note: Unaccompanied-minors facility separately reported at 2,400% of ordinary capacity by Mayor Vivas.

category: Crush and fall injuries at border breakwaters
note: Reported alongside drowning deaths at Tarajal and Benzú but no official aggregate injury count has been published.

category: Bodies recovered in weeks after peak crossing
killed: additional unconfirmed cases beyond the 111 tally
note: Some remains found in subsequent weeks have not been definitively linked to the July 30-31 crossing, leaving the final toll open.

category: Media estimate one month on (The Olive Press, Aug 30)
note: A one-month retrospective on the crisis cites 'more than 150 people died trying to reach Ceuta,' the highest figure reported to date — above both the ~111 official cumulative count and the 141 NGO (Caminando Fronteras) tally. No new recovery operation, itemised count, or official source was cited for the increase, so it may reflect rounding or re-aggregation rather than newly confirmed deaths.

category: Spanish soldier injured in migrant ambush
injured: 1 soldier (minor, struck by stone); 4 migrants also reported injured
note: Soldier struck by a stone when a military vehicle carrying four soldiers was ambushed by roughly 70 migrants in the Benzú area on Aug 27; 12 Moroccan nationals detained, of whom 11 were subsequently expelled from Ceuta on Aug 28 — the first confirmed expulsion tied directly to a violent incident since the July 30-31 crossing. First reported assault on Spanish security forces since the crossing.

category: Spanish soldier injured; migrants detained (Royal Walls stoning)
note: Four migrants detained after stoning a military patrol near Ceuta's Royal Walls in the early hours of Aug 29; a sergeant sustained a minor injury. A judge ordered the four into pretrial detention Aug 30; prosecutors seek 4 years' prison each for assault plus 2 years each for injuries, or 5-year expulsion in lieu. Second confirmed attack on security forces since the Aug 27 Benzú ambush.

category: Corrosive-liquid attack on military patrol, San Amaro
note: Three Moroccan nationals arrested by the Civil Guard for throwing bottles of corrosive liquid at a military patrol near San Amaro on Aug 30; none of the bottles struck the soldiers. Third confirmed attack on Spanish security forces during the crisis.

category: Crowd-crush injuries, Loma Colmenar shelter access
source: El Español / El Faro de Ceuta
note: Hundreds of migrants surged the entrance of the newly opened Loma Colmenar shelter after its 400-person capacity was reached on Aug 31; National Police fired warning shots and made baton charges to disperse the crowd. At least one person was injured; no official aggregate count published.

category: Police and journalists injured, Sep 2 Congress riot
injured: 4 police officers (minor); several RTVE journalists shoved, kicked or nearly headbutted
note: Roughly 50 uniformed far-right demonstrators (Núcleo Nacional) threw bottles and chairs at police outside Congress after the Sep 2 nationwide Ceuta protests wound down; officers responded with tear gas and rubber bullets, arresting 4 (2 minors). RTVE reporters covering the Madrid, Ceuta and Barcelona rallies were separately assaulted; no serious injuries reported among journalists.
